correctness.rationale: The spherical monomial integral and the radial gamma integral give the stated norm, and the torus characters of H applied to distinct monomials are distinct. Subtracting the squared norm of the analytic projection from the squared multiplication norm gives λ_α=(α₁+1)r_n−α₁r_(n−1), with the second term omitted for α₁=0. For x=(n+d)/m and a=1/m, the ratio Γ(x+a)/Γ(x) contributes 1+a(a−1)/(2x)+O(x⁻²) after factoring x^a. This gives the stated r_n expansion and its difference with r_(n−1). Multiplying that difference by α₁≤n leaves a uniform relative O(1/n), since 1−qα₁/n≥1/m. This both bounds the norm and makes the norm of the tail after truncating degrees tend to zero. With h=ε^(2/q), the high-shell lattice indicators are sandwiched by multiplicatively dilated regions with the stated angular radius; the low-degree shells disappear after the h^d normalization. The region is bounded with null radial boundary, so the lattice sum converges to its volume. The simplex Jacobian yields 1/d!, and the first-coordinate marginal is Beta(1,d−1). In the quartic d=2 case direct integration gives (1/8)·(31/80). Inversion of the positive counting asymptotic gives k s_k^p_c→C, whence the logarithmic mean and all normalized Dixmier traces equal C; strong Schatten summability fails.
